messages:
jess (support): FYI customer acme-prod is hitting a big spike of 503s on /v1/stream/generate since ~09:12 UTC. CS ticket INC-12345 created, customers seeing timeouts and retries. logs attached below. raising to oncall.

oncall-bot: New incident INC-12345 created (priority: P2) by jess (support). Paging sam (oncall).

sam (oncall): on it. can you paste a couple of request_ids and the earliest 503 timestamp?

jess (support): request_ids: r_2026-03-17T09:12:03_aa12, r_2026-03-17T09:12:45_bb34. First 503 observed 2026-03-17T09:11:58Z. attaching short logs: 

```
[09:12:02] infer-runner[24132]: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 2048MB
[09:12:03] kernel: Killed process 24132 (infer-runner) total-vm=1203452kB
[09:12:03] containerd: infer-runner-7 exited with status SIGSEGV
[09:12:04] kubelet: Started container infer-runner-7
```

maria (eng-runtime): thanks. that looks like a GPU OOM followed by a segfault during restart. we saw something similar on a prefetch regression a few weeks ago. can you grab `kubectl logs -n hosted infer-runner-7 --previous` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` from the node? also `nvidia-smi -q` snapshot.

kevin (infra): i pulled node `gpu-cc-17` events — it shows repeated OOM/KILL for container `infer-runner-7` at 09:12:03, 09:14:21. node memory/gpu utilization hit 99% at the time. logs show this kernel line: `oom_reaper killing process 24132 (infer-runner) uid 1000`

lisa (sre): pls collect core + heapdump if possible. run: 
```
kubectl -n hosted logs infer-runner-7 --previous > /tmp/infer-runner-7.prev.log
kubectl -n hosted exec infer-runner-7 -- gcore -o /tmp/core.$(date +%s) $(pidof runner)
kubectl -n hosted cp infer-runner-7:/tmp/core.* /tmp/ && gzip /tmp/core.*
```
If gcore fails (container restarts), please enable `--show-hidden-pids` and capture `/proc/*/maps` for the pid before restart.

jess (support): pasted prev logs and dmesg to the ticket. attaching small backtrace we saw in container stderr: 
```
#0  0x7f2e4d9a3bcf in llm::AttnKernel::dispatch(...) from /opt/runner/libllm.so
#1  0x7f2e4d9bb5a2 in llm::run_forward(...) from /opt/runner/libllm.so
#2  0x55a9e7f73aef in main at src/runner/main.cpp:712
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

maria (eng-runtime): those symbols align with the attention kernel. suspects: 1) a spike in sequence length or batch that causes KV cache growth + OOM, 2) a kernel bug exposed when OOM triggers a partial write. repro idea: run a streaming request with toolcall enabled and artificially high context and batch.

sam (oncall): customer impact: ~12% 503s across their traffic in last 20m, retries from client spiked cost. P95 latency jumped to 6s before failure. we've temporarily added a routing rule to fallback to `redwood/gpt-small-4k` for acme-prod while we triage. can infra cordon node gpu-cc-17 if it keeps flapping?

kevin (infra): cordoning if we see >3 restarts in 15m. for now we've drained new scheduling away from that node and marked it unschedulable for hosted infer. collecting nvml logs.

escalations: CS note: customer is asking for an RCA and a way to avoid further 503s. they also reported doubled API charges due to client retries. billing looped in.

maria (eng-runtime): short repro steps for the eng team: 
1) replicate environment: model `redwood/gpt-medium-8k-q4`, quantized runtime, batch size 16, streaming + toolcall enabled
2) send this curl to reproduce: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/stream/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-8k-q4","stream":true,"toolcall":true,"prompt":"lot of context...","max_tokens":4096,"batch_size":16}'
```
3) monitor `nvidia-smi` and `/var/log/syslog` for OOM lines. expect container restart within ~20s if hit.

lisa (sre): also capture `kv_cache_size` metric from metrics endpoint: `GET /internal/metrics?node=gpu-cc-17` — we saw a steady rise before OOM. record p95 and samples.

maria (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 
- disable KV prefetch for acme via routing override (low friction)
- reduce batch size to 8 or lower for that tenant
- deploy a hotfix that adds defensive OOM checks in the attention kernel (will need a short release)

sam (oncall): agreed. action plan: 
1) SRE: collect core/heap/dmesg/nvml (lisa + kevin) — assigned
2) Runtime: reproduce and add mitigation flag (maria) — assigned
3) Support: keep customer on fallback and monitor (jess) — assigned
4) Billing: audit retry charges and discuss credits (escalations)

deploy-bot: Rollout started for routing override `acme-prod -> redwood/gpt-small-4k` (canary 10% -> 100%).

jess (support): customer notified of fallback and suggested retry/backoff changes. they asked for ETA on runtime fix.

maria (eng-runtime): preliminary ETA for a defensive check and canary is ~6 hours, full patch + validation ~48 hours depending on repro. will update ticket when we have a repro binary.

kevin (infra): collected node snapshots, GPU process traces, and nvml logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-12345/ and linked in the ticket.

lisa (sre): marking incident as triage-complete in the ticket. next: reproduce in staging, run `ASAN` build if needed.

escalations: CS will request billing review and follow-up email to acme. leaving thread open for runtime updates. :eyes: :warning:
